messages:
incbot: PAGERDUTY -> paging maya (Oncall): Major auth errors observed from Okta in us-east-1. Alert threshold crossed for token verification failures and console login errors. Please triage. https://status.okta.com/  :rotating_light:
maya: I’m on it. seeing a spike in 401/invalid_signature from our token verifier starting ~10:12 UTC. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/789 — token verify error rate ~12% of inbound auth checks, console login errors increasing.
jordan: grabbing logs now. any upstream SLOs? is it introspect calls or JWT verification?
maya: looks like JWT verification fails where signature verification fails due to cert chain issues. Error from verifier: `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` and occasional `tls: handshake failure`. Some requests to Okta jwks endpoints are returning truncated cert chains or handshake resets.
sam: Okta status shows an edge certificate reload/handshake degradation in a subset of edge POPs. They mention TLS handshake errors with ECDSA rotations.
eli: Can we validate by curling the jwks? run: `curl -v https://dev-xxxxx.okta.com/oauth2/v1/keys`
jordan: pasted output from curl — lots of resets and occasional 200 with partial payload: ```* Connected to dev-xxxxx.okta.com (34.123.45.67) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2):
* error:1409442E:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert internal error
* Closing connection 0
```
maya: Ok. hypothesis: Okta edge is mis-serving JWKS or some CDN nodes have an incomplete cert chain -> our http client rejects on TLS validation. This causes both token verify and any server-side call relying on JWKS to fail.
tess: impact assessment — auth flows affected: interactive console SSO (users can't sign in), API traffic that validates tokens at the edge (approx 9% of API calls hitting token verify pipeline), and background jobs that refresh sessions. Customer-facing login pages show 502/SSO error for some regions.
ops-bot: Reactions: :rotating_light: x3 from SRE runbook.
jordan: mitigation options: 1) disable strict TLS verification for JWKS fetch (risky), 2) hit Okta's alternate JWKS hosts (if any), 3) serve cached JWKS and extend TTL, 4) fallback to local token introspect proxy (if available).
maya: Don't disable TLS verify. Start by enabling local cached JWKS path — we have a warmed cache from last successful rotation at 10:00 UTC. Ops: update verifier config to use `--jwks-cache-only=true` until Okta stabilizes. That will accept cached keys and only fail if kid unknown.
eli: I'm on the verifier config change. Pushing a canary to 2 verifier pods in us-east-1 now: `kubectl set env deploy/token-verifier JWKS_CACHE_ONLY=true -n prod --record`
jordan: logs from canary show token verifies succeed for old tokens, new tokens with new kid fail (kid mismatch) — expected.
sam: Customer comms: product recommends messaging impacted customers and highlighting console login degradation. How many customers affected?
tess: Early estimate: ~4% of active users in US east had console sign-in fail, but API token validation errors affected ~9% of requests; critical orgs with SAML sessions might be impacted more. We should prepare a targeted status update.
maya: Escalating to oncall manager. @sam @tess prepare a post for status.redwood.com: mention Okta TLS handshake degradation causing JWKS retrieval failures, affecting console SSO and token validation; we are serving cached keys as a mitigation.
eli: Also opening emergency support case with Okta — Case #RST-78239 created. Sharing transcript of curl failures and cert chain partials.
jordan: Workaround idea: route verification calls to Okta's alternate/data-center endpoints via our smart-routing layer — we can force verifier to resolve to different IPs (use resolver override) for a short window. Risk: DNS pinning and unforeseen path. Thoughts?
maya: Prefer caching first. If trend continues > 20% errors after 15m, escalate to routing override.
ops-bot: Runbook note appended: `if jwks retrieval failure > 10% AND Okta confirms edge TLS issue -> enable JWKS cache-only, notify customers, consider DNS override`.
sam: Draft status message in #incidents-drafts: "We’re investigating Okta TLS handshake issues impacting SSO and token validation. We've enabled cached JWKS for verification and are working with Okta. Some users may see login errors; updates forthcoming."
tess: Also flag support: create Slack triage in #support with sample org ids and affected users list so CS can proactive outreach.
eli: Pushed cache-only change to all verifier pods in us-east region. Monitoring error rate.
jordan: Error rate dropped from 12% to 2% over the last 4 minutes. Console login error pages still sporadic for some users (new tokens).
maya: Good. Next: decide on whether to extend JWKS TTL to 1hr globally as mitigation. Pro: reduces reliance on immediate jwks retrieval. Con: delays key rotation responsiveness. For now set TTL=1h in verifier only for prod regions with high errors.
sam: Approved for emergency. Implement and communicate tradeoffs to security/compliance.
eli: TTL updated. Rolling restart of verifier not required; hot-config applied.
ess: typo in plan — ignore.
maya: Okta support responded: they confirm intermittent TLS handshake failures affecting subset of edge POPs due to a mis-deployed certificate chain on their CDN nodes. They are rolling fix. ETA: 30-45m.
jordan: Plan for postmortem: capture timeline, mitigation decisions (cache-only, TTL bump, potential DNS override), impacted customers, and signal whether we should add multi-idp fallback in the long term.
sam: Agreed. Also measure % of tokens signed with new kid during window — that'll tell how many sessions will need revalidation once Okta finishes rotation.
tess: Noting customer concern: one enterprise reported admins unable to access console for 20m and had a support ticket open — CS is on it.
ops-bot: Incident severity: P1 -> decreasing to P2 after mitigation success and Okta ETA confirmed.
maya: I'll keep monitoring and will hand off when the pager is cleared. If Okta's fix doesn't show in 45m, we do DNS override plan.
eli: Monitoring graphs show slow convergence. New handshake errors trending down.
jordan: Adding this thread to postmortem tracker: https://pm.redwood.internal/incidents/2891234567
maya: handing off to night oncall @jordan at 11:20 UTC for follow-up and post-incident tasks.
jordan: taking handoff. Will validate full recovery and gather artifacts.
incbot: Incident update: P2 - mitigation implemented, Okta confirmed fix in progress. Next update scheduled in 30m.
